authorship.content_rating_notes: Moderate violence, intense romantic tension, yandere-coded psychological pressure, comedic peril. No explicit sexual content. Gore is stylized and brief.

primary.description: Continental high-fantasy setting with romantic entanglement as the primary narrative fuel. Every arc's stakes are simultaneously romantic and existential.
Imperial military academy serves as the pressure-cooker environment for all character interactions, power scaling, political intrigue, and heroine route management across eight volumes.

secondary.description: Multiple heroines develop genuine, deep emotional bonds with the protagonist. Each love is treated with sincerity and narrative weight, not as collectible trophies. The Harem True Ending is the canonical resolution, achieved through emotional authenticity rather than romantic exploitation.

The protagonist's survival-driven cowardice is systematically misread as nobility, sacrifice, and quiet genius. Every evasive maneuver deepens the misunderstanding. The comedic engine runs on the chasm between Lucen's panicked internal monologue and the world's reverent external perception.

Large-scale magical combat, continental calamity events, tournament arcs, and heroine bad-end scenarios that function as raid-boss encounters. Combat is tactically inventive but character-driven, never mechanical.
The constant proximity of death and 49 named Bad Endings played for both genuine tension and absurdist humor. The Evil Goddess's system notes provide a sardonic meta-commentary layer.

Modern Korean gamer consciousness inhabiting a doomed extra NPC within the game world. The transmigration is a one-way glitch, not a divine summoning, giving it a uniquely desperate and unsanctioned quality.

We diverge by emphasizing the protagonist's rock-bottom stats as a persistent structural constraint rather than a temporary limitation, and by delivering a planned Harem True Ending within a tighter 450-chapter framework.

protagonist_archetype_tags.description: Kang Min-jun completed 'Eschaton Hearts' across 347 hours, unlocking all 638 chapters' worth of route knowledge. His survival depends entirely on encyclopedic meta-knowledge of event flags, NPC behavior patterns, and Bad End triggers — not on combat power or charisma.

Lucen Gray possesses a Mana Index of 0.009 out of 100.000, placing him below wooden practice dummies. All combat stats are F-rank. His official academy status reads 'A person who should not exist.' He is, by every measurable metric, the weakest entity enrolled in the Solaris Imperial Academy.

Lucen's core behavioral drive is to remain invisible, avoid all named characters, and survive to graduation without triggering any story flags. He genuinely believes he is a disposable background character and acts accordingly — which is precisely why every heroine finds him extraordinary.

protagonist_archetype_tags.tag: Unreliable Self-Narrator (신뢰할 수 없는 자기 서술)
protagonist_archetype_tags.description: The comedic engine's fuel. Lucen's first-person narration frames himself as pathetic, panicking, and barely surviving. The heroine POV interludes and third-person observations reveal a young man of breathtaking courage, tactical brilliance, and quiet emotional depth. The reader holds both truths simultaneously.

Lucen survived a scripted tutorial death that should have eliminated his character. His continued existence is an ontological error in the game-world's narrative fabric, which becomes plot-critical in later volumes when the world's systems begin actively trying to correct the anomaly.

heroine_and_relationship_tags.description: Each primary heroine possesses a catastrophic Bad End transformation triggered by emotional abandonment, betrayal, or Lucen's death. Their love is genuine and deep, but the intensity scales from adorable possessiveness to continental extinction events. The yandere spectrum ranges from Iris's controlled predatory calculation to Lyra's feral draconic instinct to Alice's cheerful, smiling apocalypse.

Every primary heroine is canonically an end-game boss encounter in the original 'Eschaton Hearts' game. Their Bad End transformations are raid-tier threats. Lucen is simultaneously romancing and defusing weapons of mass destruction.

The work commits to a canonical Harem True Ending where all primary heroines' feelings are reciprocated and validated. This is not achieved through protagonist indecisiveness or harem comedy stalling, but through Lucen's genuine emotional growth and each heroine's arc reaching its authentic resolution. The True Ending is framed as the hardest, rarest achievement in the game — one that the original protagonist Lucas never unlocked.

heroine_and_relationship_tags.tag: Danger Is Romance, Romance Is Danger (위험이 로맨스, 로맨스가 위험)
heroine_and_relationship_tags.description: The work's foundational structural principle. Every romantic interaction carries genuine mortal risk. Every survival maneuver accidentally deepens romantic attachment. The two systems are inextricable and mutually escalating across all 450 chapters.

Regular perspective shifts to the heroines revealing their internal emotional landscapes, hidden traumas, growing obsession, and the vast gap between what Lucen thinks he's projecting and what they actually perceive. These interludes are the reader's primary source of dramatic irony and emotional catharsis.

system_and_world_tags.description: A catalogue of specifically titled catastrophic scenarios that Lucen must avoid. Each Bad End has a unique name, trigger condition, and consequence. They function as both comedic punchlines and genuine narrative stakes. Examples include [Bad End No. 12: The Tyrant's Curiosity], [Bad End No. 63: Skin for Love], [Bad End No. 47: Sunrise Eternal], [Bad End No. 1: A Mob's Proper Death], and [Bad End No. 49: The Stars Remember Your Name]. New Bad Ends are revealed progressively across volumes, with the final and most devastating entries unlocked only in Volumes 7 and 8.

An irregular, sardonic system interface administered by an unnamed Evil Goddess who seems to find Lucen's suffering both entertaining and endearing. System notes appear as bracketed warnings with personality: [Note: An Evil Goddess warns you to stay away from bitches at all costs!], [Note: An Evil Goddess applauds your spectacular failure.], [Note: An Evil Goddess is quietly rooting for you. Don't tell anyone.] The system provides cryptic, often deliberately misleading guidance. The Goddess's identity and true motivations become a late-stage plot revelation.

system_and_world_tags.tag: Stolen Cheat-Sheet / Hangul Notebook (빼앗긴 한글 공략 노트)
system_and_world_tags.description: Lucen's handwritten Korean-language strategy guide for surviving the game world, confiscated by Iris Aurelia during Volume 1. Because no one in the fantasy world can read Hangul, the notebook becomes a source of mystique and leverage. Iris uses it to force regular private 'decryption sessions' with Lucen, ostensibly to understand the strange script but actually to monopolize his time and attention. The notebook becomes a recurring plot device: other heroines discover its existence and compete to access it, fragments are decoded at critical moments revealing future threats, and its final pages contain Lucen's private thoughts about each heroine — a revelation saved for the climax.

The structural mechanism by which Lucen's cowardly, self-preserving actions are systematically reinterpreted by observers as acts of supreme courage, tactical genius, noble self-sacrifice, or mysterious transcendent power. The engine operates on multiple levels: heroines misread his panic as stoic resolve; nobles misread his evasion as political maneuvering; instructors misread his meta-knowledge as prodigious talent; and the original protagonist Lucas misreads his interference as the actions of a secret mentor figure. The misunderstandings compound across volumes, building an increasingly absurd and inescapable reputation.

The protagonist has entered the world of a game he completed as a speedrunner. The transmigration mechanic is specifically a 'save file glitch' — an unintended transfer into a character who was supposed to die in the tutorial. This distinguishes the work from divine-summoning or reincarnation transmigrations: Lucen's presence is unauthorized, unblessed, and structurally unstable.

system_and_world_tags.tag: Original Protagonist as Supporting Character (원래 주인공의 조연화)
system_and_world_tags.description: Lucas Ashford, the original game's golden-boy protagonist, exists as a fully realized character with his own arc, agency, and growth. He is not diminished or villainized to elevate Lucen. Instead, Lucas is earnest, competent, and likeable — but his canonical route triggers crisis flags that Lucen must covertly manage. The dynamic between the 'real' protagonist and the 'extra' who stole his narrative role is a source of both comedy and genuine pathos.

structural_and_tonal_tags.description: Solaris Imperial Academy, the continent's premier military-magical institution. Provides a contained environment for character interaction density while escalating to continental scope in later volumes.
Volume 1 stakes: survive a seating assignment. Volume 8 stakes: rewrite the cosmological ending of reality. The escalation is continuous and organic, never resetting.

The work oscillates rapidly between laugh-out-loud comedic misunderstandings and genuinely harrowing emotional stakes. The tonal whiplash is intentional and precisely controlled, creating a reading rhythm that keeps audiences emotionally engaged across hundreds of chapters.
35-45% of total word count is dialogue. Conversations drive plot, reveal character, and deliver comedy simultaneously. Long descriptive passages are avoided in favor of rapid, punchy exchanges.

1-3 sentences per paragraph maximum. Generous white space between paragraphs. This pacing creates comedic timing through visual rhythm — the gap between paragraphs functions like the beat before a punchline.

volume_breakdown.arc_summary: Kang Min-jun awakens as Lucen Gray moments before his scripted tutorial death. He survives the glitch, enrolls in Solaris Imperial Academy, and desperately tries to remain invisible. Seat assignments place him beside Iris Aurelia. The first evaluation test exposes his 0.009 Mana Index. His Hangul notebook is confiscated. By chapter 50, three heroines have fixated on him and five Bad Ends have been narrowly avoided.

The Grand Academy Festival brings external nobles, visiting dignitaries, and catastrophic event flags. Lucen covertly intervenes in three crisis scenarios while participating in mock duels he desperately tries to lose. His 'losses' are interpreted as masterful restraint. Misunderstandings expand from the heroine circle to the entire student body. Rhea Valtor enters the heroine rotation. Lucas Ashford begins to notice the strange extra who keeps appearing at every crisis point.

The longest volume. Midterm examinations and the discovery of the Abyssal Library beneath the academy. This volume is heavy on Heroine POV Interludes, revealing each heroine's hidden trauma, canonical fate, and the precise emotional mechanism by which they've become obsessed with Lucen. Alice's true identity as Celestia Rimehart is partially exposed. Lyra Silverclaw transfers in as a junior cadet, introducing draconic politics. Lucen's reputation as a 'mysterious genius who hides his power' becomes entrenched campus legend. The volume ends with the first genuine near-death experience that Lucen cannot laugh off.
volume_breakdown.stakes_ceiling: Ancient sealed evil beneath the academy and heroine emotional breaking points

volume_breakdown.arc_summary: The Emperor summons Lucen to the Imperial Palace for a banquet that is actually a political interrogation. Multiple heroines independently threaten faculty, nobles, and imperial guards to accompany or protect him. The palace arc expands the world beyond the academy, revealing continental power structures, the Church's hidden agenda, and the Chancellor's growing unease about an extra who keeps disrupting canonical events. Heroine jealousy dynamics reach their first major boiling point in a legendary banquet scene where four heroines simultaneously claim Lucen as their escort. The volume concludes with the Emperor offering Lucen a position that would make it impossible for him to remain a mob character.
volume_breakdown.stakes_ceiling: Imperial politics, heroine factional warfare, and the Chancellor's suspicion

volume_breakdown.arc_summary: Continental Calamity Invasions begin — the canonical mid-game crises that destroy nations in the original game's bad routes. Lucen saves heroines from their canonical deaths, each rescue deepening emotional bonds to the point of no return. This is the volume where comedic distance begins to collapse: the heroines' feelings become undeniably real to Lucen, and his own feelings — which he has denied for 300 chapters — begin to surface. Intimate emotional scenes replace comedic misunderstandings as the primary relationship driver, though the misunderstanding engine still operates at the macro level with nations and organizations.
volume_breakdown.stakes_ceiling: Continental destruction, heroine canonical death flags, and Lucen's emotional walls cracking

volume_breakdown.arc_summary: A continental tournament brings together representatives from every nation and academy. Lucen is forced to participate publicly for the first time, making mob-character anonymity permanently impossible. The tournament arc serves as a vehicle for unmasking the Chancellor's treason and the Church's secret alliance with the entity behind the Calamity Invasions. Rhea's combat arc reaches its zenith. Lucas Ashford and Lucen fight side by side for the first time, with Lucas finally understanding that the 'extra' has been protecting everyone from the shadows all along.
volume_breakdown.stakes_ceiling: Public exposure, political treason, and theological conspiracy

volume_breakdown.arc_summary: The Continental Extinction Event triggers — the original game's final act. Every unresolved Bad End flag converges. Heroines begin transforming toward their catastrophic final-boss states as hope collapses. Lucen must simultaneously prevent the end of the world and prevent each heroine from becoming the instrument of that end. This is the darkest volume: characters die (temporarily), alliances shatter, and Lucen's identity as a transmigrator is exposed to the heroines. The volume ends on the most devastating cliffhanger: Bad End No. 49 activates, and the Evil Goddess's system goes silent.
volume_breakdown.bad_ends_introduced: No. 49: The Stars Remember Your Name (the final and most catastrophic Bad End)
volume_breakdown.stakes_ceiling: Continental extinction, heroine boss transformations, and transmigrator identity exposure

volume_breakdown.arc_summary: The shortest and most emotionally dense volume. Lucen, with 0.009 mana and no divine blessing, achieves what 347 hours of speedrunning told him was impossible: the Harem True Ending. Not through power, but through the accumulated weight of 440 chapters of genuine human connection. Each heroine's resolution is given its own chapter. The Evil Goddess reveals her identity in the penultimate chapter. The final chapter is Lucen's epilogue — an ordinary morning in an extraordinary world, surrounded by terrifying women who love him completely, still insisting he's just a mob character.
volume_breakdown.bad_ends_introduced: None. All 49 Bad Ends are resolved or transcended.
volume_breakdown.stakes_ceiling: Cosmological rewrite and the validation of every emotional bond across the entire work

unique_selling_propositions.usp: The Weakest Protagonist in the Genre — Permanently
unique_selling_propositions.detail: Lucen's 0.009 Mana Index never increases. He does not gain a hidden cheat power, a late-game awakening, or a divine blessing. His F-rank stats are his F-rank stats at chapter 1 and chapter 450. The victory condition is achieved entirely through meta-knowledge, emotional intelligence, and the accumulated bonds of 440 chapters. This is a structural commitment, not a temporary handicap.

unique_selling_propositions.usp: 49 Named Bad Endings as a Catalogued Threat System
unique_selling_propositions.detail: Each Bad End is specifically titled, numbered, and described, creating a collectible threat taxonomy that readers can track and anticipate. The progressive revelation of new Bad Ends across volumes creates a persistent secondary tension layer beneath the primary narrative.

Regularly scheduled perspective shifts to heroines transform what could be a standard misunderstanding comedy into a dual-layered emotional experience. Readers simultaneously laugh at Lucen's panicked narration and ache at the heroines' sincere, desperate love.

The work executes a deliberate tonal evolution from comedy-dominant (Volumes 1-3) through balanced (Volumes 4-5) to drama-dominant (Volumes 6-8) without losing its comedic identity. The misunderstanding engine continues operating at the macro level even as individual relationships achieve emotional honesty.

The Harem True Ending is positioned as the rarest, hardest achievement — one the original game protagonist never unlocked. It is earned through 450 chapters of genuine character development, not narrative convenience. Each heroine's resolution is given dedicated narrative space and emotional weight.

metadata.reference_work: 로맨스 판타지 게임에서 살아남는 법 (How to Survive in the Romance Fantasy Game)
metadata.adaptation_scope: Full 638-chapter reference scope compressed and restructured into a tighter 450-chapter / 8-volume architecture. All major arcs, character dynamics, and thematic elements are preserved. Compression is achieved through elimination of filler arcs and tighter pacing, not through cutting heroine development or emotional payoffs.
